title: Stability anchor calibration for INT8/FP16 embedding profiles + cosine similarity monitoring
creator: Maya Thomsen
description: Create a repeatable calibration and monitoring flow that produces production-ready INT8 and FP16 embedding quantization profiles while controlling semantic drift. The approach introduces 'stability anchors' (small curated reference corpora + layer-scale anchors) used during calibration and periodic validation to bound cosine-similarity regressions relative to an FP32 baseline. Deliverables: calibration harness, calibrated profile artifacts, validation notebooks, canary rollout automation, and dashboard alerts that trigger recalibration or rollback when drift thresholds are exceeded.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness can generate INT8 and FP16 profile artifacts for target embedding models and store artifacts in S3 with metadata
Validation pipeline computes paired-cosine distributions against FP32 baseline and produces a summary report (median, p90, p95, tail failure rate)
Quantized profile performance meets gating thresholds on held-out corpora (see metrics) for median and tail behavior
Canary rollout automation can route 5% traffic to quantized variant and automatically rollback if monitored thresholds breach
Dashboard tile for embed-quant stability added to Console with historical trend and alerts wired to PagerDuty
experiment_plan: Select 4 stability anchor corpora: internal-recall-v1, public-ms-marco-subset, chatlog-synthetic, embeddings-eval-1k
For each corpus sample 50k source embeddings and produce FP32 baseline embeddings
Run layerwise calibration sweep: per-layer scale + global scale search for INT8 and FP16 quant rules
Evaluate paired-cosine distribution between FP32 and quantized embeddings across corpora and compute retrieval metrics (top-k recall, MRR)
Tune gating thresholds by sweeping on validation corpora to tradeoff cost vs. accuracy, record profile metadata
Perform a 5% canary in staging for 48 hours with tracing enabled and compare live metrics to baseline
metrics: top1 recall drop <= 0.2 percentage points relative to baseline
embedding generation latency overhead relative to CPU quant path <= 5%
unit cost improvement (tokens/tokenized embed) tracked for ROI analysis
runbook: Calibration: python tools/calibrate_embeddings.py --model xlarge-embed --mode int8 --corpus s3://redwood-anchor/internal-recall-v1 --out s3://redwood-calib/ENG-52678/int8-profile.json
Compute paired-cosine: python tools/compare_embeddings.py --pairs reports/ENG-52678/pairs.parquet --metrics reports/ENG-52678/metrics.csv
Canary rollout: console route creation 'embed-xlarge-quant-int8-canary' 5% traffic, enable trace-id tagging and drift metrics, monitoring window 48h
Rollback: console route update to switch canary back to baseline and run a postmortem collection script tools/collect_postmortem.sh
results_summary: Pilot run on 'internal-recall-v1' (50k pairs) with the first INT8 candidate showed median cosine delta = 0.0028, p95 = 0.018, but tail fraction (delta < -0.05) = 0.12% which exceeds the target 0.1%. Top1 retrieval drop measured at 0.14pp. FP16 profile performed within all thresholds. Action: perform per-layer re-anchoring to reduce tail regressions and re-run the sweep on the chatlog and MS-MARCO subsets.
